business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 Business ([P1]) and 10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Resolute Holdings Management, Inc. provides operating management services to GPGI Holdings, L.L.C. and, as of January 12, 2026, Husky Holdings LLC to generate recurring, long-duration management fees, and owns no equity in GPGI Holdings, Husky Holdings, or GPGI, Inc.
quotes: It is organized to provide operating management services to GPGI Holdings, L.L.C. (formerly CompoSecure Holdings, L.L.C.) (“GPGI Holdings”) and as of January 12, 2026, Husky Holdings LLC (“Husky Holdings”), and other companies it may manage in the future, both in the United States and internationally, to generate recurring, long-duration management fees.
Resolute Holdings does not own any equity interests or common stock in GPGI Holdings, Husky Holdings, or GPGI, Inc. (formerly CompoSecure, Inc.) (“GPGI”).

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Under the CompoSecure Management Agreement and the substantially identical Husky Management Agreement, each managed company pays a quarterly cash management fee equal to 2.5% of its last 12 months' Management Agreement Adjusted EBITDA (without duplication of the other or Parent Allocated Expense), under agreements with an initial term of 10 years and automatic ten-year renewals.
quotes: Pursuant to the CompoSecure Management Agreement, GPGI Holdings pays Resolute Holdings a quarterly management fee (the “CompoSecure Management Fee”), payable in arrears, in a cash amount equal to 2.5% of GPGI Holdings’ last 12 months’ Adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the CompoSecure Management Agreement, measured for the period ending on the fiscal quarter then ended (“CompoSecure Management Agreement Adjusted EBITDA”).
The CompoSecure Management Agreement has an initial term of 10 years and shall automatically renew for successive ten-year terms unless terminated in accordance with its terms.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q Part I Item 2 MD&A ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Because the CompoSecure Management Agreement makes Resolute Holdings the primary beneficiary of GPGI Holdings under ASC 810, Resolute Holdings consolidates GPGI Holdings and its subsidiary Husky Holdings, eliminating management fee revenue in consolidation so that consolidated net sales reflect product and service sales of CompoSecure and Husky.
quotes: In accordance with ASC 810 and due to the terms of the CompoSecure Management Agreement, as defined below, Resolute Holdings (together with GPGI Holdings and its subsidiary, Husky Holdings, the “Company”) is required to consolidate GPGI Holdings because it is a variable interest entity (“VIE”) of which Resolute Holdings is deemed to be the primary beneficiary.

Net sales reflect the Company’s revenue generated from the sale of products and services by GPGI Holdings’ businesses, CompoSecure and Husky, as management fee revenue at Resolute Holdings is eliminated in consolidation.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 ([P1]), 10-K Item 7 ([P3]), and 10-Q Part I Item 2 ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Through CompoSecure, the consolidated Company designs and manufactures premium metal payment cards (contact, dual interface, and Arculus authentication cards), Prelams, and secure authentication solutions for card issuer customers, and sells Arculus key cards direct-to-consumer via third-party e-commerce platforms.
quotes: Net sales at CompoSecure primarily include the design and manufacturing of metal cards, including contact and dual interface cards and cards containing Arculus authentication capability, and direct-to-consumer sales of Arculus key cards through third-party e-commerce platforms.

GPGI Holdings also generates revenue from the sale of Prelams (which refers to pre-laminated, sub-assemblies consisting of a composite of material layers which are partially laminated to be used as a component in the multiple layers of a final payment card or other card construction).

CompoSecure’s metal cards deliver a distinctive weight, a premium aesthetic, and enhanced durability for consumers, while its issuer customers benefit from the ability to attract higher-value consumers, reduce cardholder churn, and unlock higher customer spend relative to traditional plastic cards.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 ([P1]) and 10-Q Part I Item 2 ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Through Husky, the consolidated Company manufactures injection molding machines, molds, hot runners, temperature controllers, auxiliary equipment, and medical molds, and sells aftermarket parts and lifecycle services to customers across food, beverage, medical device, packaging, closures, and consumer product applications.
quotes: Husky has focused on developing highly technical precision technologies instrumental in the delivery of food, beverages, medical devices, and other applications including general packaging and closures, thinwall packaging, and consumer products.

Net sales at Husky include the sale of injection molding machines, molds, hot runners, temperature controllers, auxiliary equipment, and related aftermarket products; the design and manufacture of medical molds; service offerings including startup, testing, installation, training, ongoing monitoring of machines, and extended protection plans.

The increase was driven by a 16% increase in domestic sales in GPGI Holdings’ premium payment card business, partially offset by international sales which were down 19%.
The increase was due to higher volumes from new and existing customers and a higher blended average selling price.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q Part I Item 2 ([P4]) and Part II Item 1A Risk Factors ([P5]).
business_model.claim: Trade policies, inflationary pressures, higher input costs, and hostilities in the Middle East have increased costs for customers and caused existing customers to pause or delay orders and prospective customers to defer new projects, reducing product demand.
quotes: These conditions have increased costs for our customers and caused existing customers to pause or delay orders and prospective customers to defer new projects.

For example, long-term market uncertainty, economic impacts driven by trade policies and inflationary pressures, and higher input costs have reduced demand for the Company's products and led to shipping and payment delays.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 7 ([P3]) and 10-Q Part I Item 2 ([P4]).
business_model.claim: Consolidated cost of sales comprises GPGI Holdings' direct and indirect manufacturing and service costs—including raw materials such as metals, labor, equipment and facilities, overhead, depreciation and amortization, leases, shipping, and freight—and is driven by volume, operational efficiencies (including the Resolute Operating System), procurement costs, and promotional activity.
quotes: Product costs include the cost of raw materials and supplies, including various metals; the cost of labor; equipment and facilities; operational overhead; depreciation and amortization; leases and rental charges; shipping and handling; and freight and insurance costs.
Cost of sales can be impacted by many factors, including volume, operational efficiencies, procurement costs, and promotional activity.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q Part I Item 2 ([P4]) and Part II Item 1A Risk Factors ([P5]).

quotes: Ongoing geopolitical tensions and hostilities in the Middle East have contributed to higher global oil prices and disruptions in international shipping, which have increased our shipping and logistics costs as well as the costs of certain raw materials.

These impacts have included and may continue to include decreased sales; supply chain and logistics disruptions; volatility in foreign exchange rates and interest rates; inflationary pressures on and availability of raw materials and energy; and heightened cybersecurity threats.

competitive_position.claim: Resolute Holdings operates a capital-light management model with 7 full-time employees at the parent entity, earning quarterly fees equal to 2.5% of each managed company's last 12 months' Adjusted EBITDA without owning equity in the managed businesses.
quotes: Resolute Holdings (together with GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings, the “Company”) only receives management fees from GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings and does not own any equity interests including common stock in GPGI Holdings, Husky Holdings, or GPGI.

As of February 1, 2026, the Company had approximately 5,534 full-time employees and 86 part-time employees consisting of 971 full-time employees and 6 part-time employees at CompoSecure, 4,556 full-time employees and 80 part-time employees at Husky, and 7 full-time employees at Resolute Holdings.

Pursuant to the CompoSecure Management Agreement, GPGI Holdings pays Resolute Holdings a quarterly management fee (the “CompoSecure Management Fee”), payable in arrears, in a cash amount equal to 2.5% of GPGI Holdings’ last 12 months’ Adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the CompoSecure Management Agreement, measured for the period ending on the fiscal quarter then ended (“CompoSecure Management Agreement Adjusted EBITDA”).

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P4
competitive_position.claim: Both the CompoSecure Management Agreement and the Husky Management Agreement carry an initial term of 10 years with automatic renewal for successive 10-year periods and termination-fee rights under certain limited events.
quotes: The CompoSecure Management Agreement has an initial term of 10 years and shall automatically renew for successive ten-year terms unless terminated in accordance with its terms.
The Husky Management Agreement has an initial term of 10 years and shall automatically renew for successive ten-year terms unless terminated in accordance with its terms.

Additionally, following the initial term of the respective management agreement, the management fees payable to us thereunder could be reduced, including upon an election by us not to receive our management fee for a given quarterly period.

competitive_position.claim: CompoSecure holds a leading global position in designing and manufacturing premium metal payment cards and secure authentication solutions, supported by materials science, proprietary manufacturing processes, and payment-network certifications.
quotes: CompoSecure, founded in 2000, and headquartered in Somerset, New Jersey, is the global leader in the design and manufacturing of premium metal payment cards and secure authentication solutions.

The company pioneered the use of metal in payment cards dating back to 2003 and combines industry-leading innovation, advanced materials science, and proprietary manufacturing processes to deliver highly differentiated products to its customers.

competitive_position.claim: CompoSecure's metal payment cards give card issuers differentiated consumer appeal that helps attract higher-value consumers, reduce cardholder churn, and unlock higher customer spend than plastic cards.
quotes: CompoSecure’s metal cards deliver a distinctive weight, a premium aesthetic, and enhanced durability for consumers, while its issuer customers benefit from the ability to attract higher-value consumers, reduce cardholder churn, and unlock higher customer spend relative to traditional plastic cards.

competitive_position.claim: Husky holds a leading global position in manufacturing highly engineered injection molding equipment, combining systems, tooling, and aftermarket parts and services across the customer lifecycle.
quotes: Husky, founded in 1953, and headquartered in Bolton, Ontario, is the leading global manufacturer of highly engineered injection molding equipment and aftermarket tooling and services.

Husky delivers its integrated capabilities through a combination of systems, tooling, and aftermarket parts and services to create value for customers throughout the entire lifecycle of its solutions.

competitive_position.claim: Completing the Husky acquisition expanded the platform's market and revenue diversification, increased its operating scale, and reduced customer concentration.
quotes: The Husky Transaction was completed on January 12, 2026 (“Husky Transaction Date”) and provides the Company with market and revenue diversification, increased scale, and reduces customer concentration.

competitive_position.claim: Consolidated net sales rose 10% to $462.1 million on 16% domestic growth (partially offset by a 19% international decline), while gross profit margin expanded 4% to 56% through volume, mix, and Resolute Operating System execution.
quotes: The Company’s net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $41.5 million to $462.1 million compared to $420.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
The increase was driven by a 16% increase in domestic sales in GPGI Holdings’ premium payment card business, partially offset by international sales which were down 19%.

The Company’s gross profit for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $41.0 million, or 19%, to $260.2 million compared to $219.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, while the gross profit margin increased by 4% to 56%.
The increase was driven by higher volumes, mix, and improved operational execution from the implementation of the Resolute Operating System.

competitive_position.claim: On a standalone segment basis, Resolute Holdings' quarterly management fees grew from $3.7 to $13.8 (table in millions) and Non-GAAP Fee-Related Earnings rose from $1.1 to $5.5 (table in millions) against a relatively fixed operating expense base of 4.0 and 4.2 (table in millions).
quotes: This presentation of financial results does not represent the underlying economics or the positive attributes of Resolute Holdings’ standalone business model, which consist of recurring, long-duration management fees and a relatively fixed expense base.

The increase in Non-GAAP profitability was driven by the higher fee stream as a result of the execution of the management agreement with Husky Holdings LLC (“Husky Holdings”) in January 2026, along with organic growth in fees from the CompoSecure management agreement.

competitive_position.claim: Including Husky following its acquisition, consolidated net sales expanded from $ 344.3 to $ 1,390.6 (table in millions) for the year-to-date period and from $ 120.9 to $ 509.6 (table in millions) for the quarterly period.
quotes: Management’s discussion and analysis of the Company’s financial condition and results of operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 only includes the results of Husky Holdings from the completion of the Husky Transaction on January 12, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Resolute Holdings' revenues are highly concentrated in fees from GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings until additional management agreements are signed, exposing results to underperformance, termination, or fee reductions at either managed company.
quotes: As a result, for so long as our only management agreements are the CompoSecure Management Agreement and the Husky Management Agreement, our revenues will be dependent on the management fees and other payments we receive from our two managed companies, GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings.

The termination of any management agreement, including the CompoSecure Management Agreement or the Husky Management Agreement, or the reduction of fees payable to us thereunder, would each have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Resolute Holdings faces intense competition when pursuing additional management agreements from institutional investors, private equity, hedge, and investment funds that may acquire targets outright and have greater resources, longer histories, stronger relationships, and better funding access.
quotes: We expect to face significant competition in identifying potential additional managed companies from a variety of other entities, including institutional investors and private equity, hedge and investment funds.

Additionally, these competitors may have, among other things, greater resources, longer operating histories, more established relationships, greater expertise, better reputations, better access to funding, different regulatory barriers and different risk tolerances than we do.

competitive_position.claim: Resolute Holdings has a limited operating history in an unproven public-company fee-management model and is heavily dependent on key executives David Cote and Tom Knott, alongside potential time-allocation and incentive conflicts.
quotes: Additionally, our management team has not previously sponsored or managed a company whose business is based on the generation of fees from the long-term management of public companies across multiple industries, sectors and geographies.

Our future success depends to a significant extent on the continued service and coordination of our personnel, including our senior management team, particularly David Cote, our Executive Chairman, and Tom Knott, our Chief Executive Officer.
Additionally, our management members’ other commitments may result in a conflict of interest in allocating their time between our operations and our management and operations of other businesses.

The CompoSecure Management Agreement and Husky Management Agreement provide, and we expect that any management agreements we enter into with additional managed companies in the future will provide, for a management fee based on profitability metrics defined in each such management agreement, and these fees may impact our management priorities or cause us to select riskier managed company businesses.

competitive_position.claim: CompoSecure's competitive position is threatened by customer retention risk, new-product commercialization delays, supply chain and manufacturing quality disruptions, uncertain Arculus authentication adoption, and digital-asset regulatory restrictions.
quotes: Failure to retain existing customers or identify and attract new customers could adversely affect the business, financial condition and results of operations of the CompoSecure business.

Security markets, including the market for authentication solutions, are rapidly evolving to address increasing and challenging cyber threats, including identity theft, and the CompoSecure business’ Arculus Authenticate solutions may not achieve widespread market acceptance.

Regulatory changes or actions may restrict the use of the Arculus Cold Storage Wallet or digital assets in a manner that adversely affects the business, prospects or operations of the CompoSecure business.
Production quality and manufacturing process disruptions could adversely affect the CompoSecure business.

competitive_position.claim: Husky's competitive position is threatened by unpredictable customer purchasing trends, emerging-market volatility, raw material price fluctuations, supplier delivery failures, foreign-jurisdiction operating risks, and taxes or regulations targeting beverage consumption.
quotes: The results of operations of the Husky business are reliant on unpredictable customer purchasing trends.
There is no certainty that the Husky business will be able to manage fluctuations in raw materials.
Failure of suppliers to deliver in a timely and cost-effective manner would adversely impact its operations.
The significant international operations of the Husky business subject it to risks inherent in doing business in foreign jurisdictions.
New or increased taxes or other governmental regulations targeted to decrease the consumption of certain type of beverages may adversely affect the Husky business.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3, P4, and P5
competitive_position.claim: Trade policies including U.S. tariffs, foreign raw material reliance, inflationary input pressures, and geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine have raised shipping and material costs, constrained supply chains, and led customers to delay orders or defer projects.
quotes: Ongoing geopolitical tensions and hostilities in the Middle East have contributed to higher global oil prices and disruptions in international shipping, which have increased our shipping and logistics costs as well as the costs of certain raw materials.
These conditions have increased costs for our customers and caused existing customers to pause or delay orders and prospective customers to defer new projects.

For example, long-term market uncertainty, economic impacts driven by trade policies and inflationary pressures, and higher input costs have reduced demand for the Company's products and led to shipping and payment delays.

competitive_position.claim: Growth at the managed companies is exposed to M&A integration risks and uncertain capital-market funding access, while complex VIE accounting and potential litigation or government proceedings could impair results or reduce management fees.
quotes: Our ability to expand their businesses is subject to a number of risks, including the inability to identify satisfactory strategic acquisition targets, difficulties in successfully integrating acquired operations and businesses, loss of key personnel, diversion of management resources, financial risks including unanticipated liabilities and incremental compliance costs due to the acquisition of businesses subject to heavy regulation and risks associated with achieving cost synergies.

Such funding may not be available on terms favorable or acceptable to us or at all, which could limit our managed companies’ ability to undertake these business activities, and which in turn could materially adversely impact our ability to successfully pursue our strategy of growth.

If such proceedings are determined adversely to us or to our managed companies, we may be required to change our business practices or we may incur fines, penalties or monetary losses, some of which may be significant or could disrupt the operation of our business, and the financial performance of our managed companies may be adversely impacted, which may reduce our management fees.

The Company anticipates that to the extent GPGI Holdings requires additional liquidity, it shall do so through borrowings on its revolving credit facility, the incurrence of other indebtedness, or a combination thereof and offering of GPGI shares in capital markets.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release [P6] and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A [P4].
growth_thesis.claim: Resolute Holdings grew standalone management fees from $3.7 (table in millions) to $13.8 (table in millions) and diluted Non-GAAP Fee-Related Earnings per share from $0.13 to $0.69 year over year in the fiscal third quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by adding the Husky Management Agreement (2.5% of Husky Holdings' last twelve months' Adjusted EBITDA) alongside organic fee growth from CompoSecure.
quotes: The increase in Non-GAAP profitability was driven by the higher fee stream as a result of the execution of the management agreement with Husky Holdings LLC (“Husky Holdings”) in January 2026, along with organic growth in fees from the CompoSecure management agreement.

In conjunction with the closing of the Husky Transaction, Husky Holdings and Resolute Holdings entered into a management agreement (the “Husky Management Agreement”) on substantially identical terms as the CompoSecure Management Agreement (as described above), pursuant to which Resolute Holdings provides management and other related services to Husky Holdings in exchange for payment of a quarterly management fee (“Husky Management Fee”), payable in arrears, in a cash amount equal to 2.5% of Husky Holdings’ last twelve months' Adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the Husky Management Agreement, measured for the period ending on the fiscal quarter then ended (“Husky Management Agreement Adjusted EBITDA”).

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors [P2] and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A [P4].
growth_thesis.claim: Continuing fee growth from adding new managed companies requires identifying and signing additional agreements despite significant competition from institutional investors and private equity, hedge, and investment funds, conducting effective due diligence, and avoiding termination or fee reductions under the initial 10-year CompoSecure and Husky agreements.
quotes: The successful expansion of our business may depend on our ability to identify additional companies with which to enter into agreements to manage their respective businesses in return for the payment to us of management fees and to effectively manage such additional businesses.

We expect to face significant competition in identifying potential additional managed companies from a variety of other entities, including institutional investors and private equity, hedge and investment funds.

The termination of any management agreement, including the CompoSecure Management Agreement or the Husky Management Agreement, or the reduction of fees payable to us thereunder, would each have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Business [P1] and MD&A [P3].
growth_thesis.claim: Organic growth in management fees (2.5% of last 12 months' Adjusted EBITDA) is driven by deploying the Resolute Operating System and underlying commercial performance at managed businesses, which in 2025 helped lift CompoSecure-era net sales by 10% to $462.1 million and gross profit by 19% to $260.2 million (56% gross margin).
quotes: Resolute Holdings applies a differentiated approach of value creation through the systematic deployment of the Resolute Operating System (“ROS”) to drive performance at businesses it manages with the intention of creating value at both the underlying managed businesses and at Resolute Holdings.
The Company’s net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $41.5 million to $462.1 million compared to $420.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The Company’s gross profit for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $41.0 million, or 19%, to $260.2 million compared to $219.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, while the gross profit margin increased by 4% to 56%.
The increase was driven by higher volumes, mix, and improved operational execution from the implementation of the Resolute Operating System.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors [P2] and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A [P4] and Risk Factors [P5].
growth_thesis.claim: For organic fee growth at CompoSecure and Husky to continue, both businesses must retain and attract customers, commercialize new products (including Arculus Authenticate), maintain reliable supply chains, and overcome tariff, inflationary, and geopolitical headwinds (including the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran) that have reduced demand and caused customer order, shipping, and payment delays.
quotes: These fees are based on the quarterly performance of the CompoSecure and Husky businesses, and accordingly, our business is subject to the business risks of CompoSecure and Husky, and may be significantly adversely affected if either business performs poorly or does not perform as expected.
These conditions have increased costs for our customers and caused existing customers to pause or delay orders and prospective customers to defer new projects.

For example, long-term market uncertainty, economic impacts driven by trade policies and inflationary pressures, and higher input costs have reduced demand for the Company's products and led to shipping and payment delays.

The intensity and duration of conflicts in the Middle East, including the recent conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran, and the potential for the expansion of hostilities in the region, are difficult to predict and could further disrupt the Company's supply chains and operations, which could have a negative impact on the Company's results of operations.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q income statement [F2], 2025 Form 10-K Business [P1], and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A [P4].
growth_thesis.claim: Resolute Holdings applies M&A and capital markets expertise to drive inorganic expansion of its managed businesses, exemplified by GPGI's approximately $4.976 billion Husky Transaction on January 12, 2026, which contributed to consolidated net sales rising from $ 120.9 (table in millions) to $ 509.6 (table in millions) in the three months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Resolute Holdings also applies its M&A and capital markets expertise to drive inorganic growth of its managed businesses.

On November 2, 2025, GPGI entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with entities affiliated with Platinum Equity, LLC (“Platinum Equity”) pursuant to which GPGI would combine with Husky Technologies Limited for aggregate consideration of approximately $4.976 billion, comprised of cash and shares of GPGI’s Class A Common Stock (the “Husky Transaction”).

Management’s discussion and analysis of the Company’s financial condition and results of operations for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 only includes the results of Husky Holdings from the completion of the Husky Transaction on January 12, 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors [P2].
growth_thesis.claim: Continued inorganic growth of GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings requires identifying satisfactory strategic targets, integrating acquired operations and achieving cost synergies, and raising additional equity or debt financing on acceptable terms.
quotes: Additionally, for so long as our managed companies consist solely or primarily of GPGI Holdings and Husky Holdings, our growth prospects will be substantially dependent on our ability to effectively manage and expand the businesses owned by these entities, including by successfully identifying, negotiating, completing and integrating strategic acquisitions.

Such funding may not be available on terms favorable or acceptable to us or at all, which could limit our managed companies’ ability to undertake these business activities, and which in turn could materially adversely impact our ability to successfully pursue our strategy of growth.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release text and standalone segment table [P6].
growth_thesis.claim: Resolute Holdings' standalone earnings exhibit operating leverage over a relatively fixed expense base: in the three months ended September 30, 2026 versus the prior-year period, segment management fees increased from $3.7 to $13.8 (table in millions) while segment operating expenses rose from 4.0 to 4.2 (table in millions), turning segment operating income from (0.3) to 9.6 and Non-GAAP Fee-Related Earnings from $1.1 to $5.5 (table in millions).
quotes: This presentation of financial results does not represent the underlying economics or the positive attributes of Resolute Holdings’ standalone business model, which consist of recurring, long-duration management fees and a relatively fixed expense base.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Business [P1], Risk Factors [P2], and MD&A [P3].
growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining standalone operating leverage and strategy execution requires retaining key leaders David Cote and Tom Knott, keeping personnel and third-party diligence expenses contained as the team scales from 7 full-time Resolute Holdings employees (as of February 1, 2026), and receiving timely cash fee payments from managed companies.
quotes: As of February 1, 2026, the Company had approximately 5,534 full-time employees and 86 part-time employees consisting of 971 full-time employees and 6 part-time employees at CompoSecure, 4,556 full-time employees and 80 part-time employees at Husky, and 7 full-time employees at Resolute Holdings.

Our future success depends to a significant extent on the continued service and coordination of our personnel, including our senior management team, particularly David Cote, our Executive Chairman, and Tom Knott, our Chief Executive Officer.

Furthermore, competition for experienced management personnel could require us to pay higher compensation and provide additional benefits to retain or attract qualified personnel, which could result in higher compensation expenses for us.
Resolute Holdings is dependent on payment of the management fees from its managed companies to maintain sufficient liquidity.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q balance sheet [F1], cash flow statement [F3], and Form 8-K Item 8.01 [P7].

quotes: Resolute Holdings Management, Inc. (“Resolute Holdings”) is a Nevada corporation that was originally formed as a Delaware corporation on September 27, 2024 (“Inception Date”) and was recently redomiciled to the State of Nevada on March 2, 2026.

material_events.claim: GPGI Holdings' previously outstanding Exchangeable Notes were exchanged for shares of GPGI Class A common stock and extinguished.
quotes: The decrease in other expense was primarily due to lower interest expense as a result of the previously outstanding Exchangeable Notes of GPGI Holdings being exchanged for shares of GPGI Class A common stock and extinguished during the fourth quarter of 2024.

material_events.claim: GPGI completed the Spin-Off by distributing all shares of Resolute Holdings common stock on a pro rata basis to holders of GPGI Class A Common Stock of record, and Resolute Holdings began regular-way trading on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the ticker RHLD.
quotes: On February 28, 2025, GPGI distributed all shares of common stock of its wholly owned subsidiary, Resolute Holdings, on a pro rata basis to the holders of GPGI’s Class A Common Stock as of the February 20, 2025 record date (“Spin-Off”).
On February 28, 2025, Resolute Holdings started trading regular-way on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the ticker symbol “RHLD”.

material_events.claim: In connection with the Spin-Off, Resolute Holdings entered into the CompoSecure Management Agreement with GPGI Holdings for a quarterly management fee equal to 2.5% of GPGI Holdings' last 12 months' Adjusted EBITDA and an initial term of 10 years, requiring Resolute Holdings to consolidate GPGI Holdings as a variable interest entity.
quotes: In connection with the completion of the Spin-Off, Resolute Holdings entered into a management agreement with GPGI Holdings (the “CompoSecure Management Agreement”), pursuant to which Resolute Holdings is responsible for managing the day-to-day business and operations and overseeing the strategy of GPGI Holdings and its controlled affiliates.
Due to the execution of and the terms of the CompoSecure Management Agreement, Resolute Holdings is required to consolidate GPGI Holdings for financial reporting purposes.

Pursuant to the CompoSecure Management Agreement, GPGI Holdings pays Resolute Holdings a quarterly management fee (the “CompoSecure Management Fee”), payable in arrears, in a cash amount equal to 2.5% of GPGI Holdings’ last 12 months’ Adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the CompoSecure Management Agreement, measured for the period ending on the fiscal quarter then ended (“Management Agreement Adjusted EBITDA”).
The CompoSecure Management Agreement has an initial term of 10 years and shall automatically renew for successive ten-year terms unless terminated in accordance with its terms.

material_events.claim: Resolute Holdings transferred the listing of its common stock from Nasdaq to the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol RHLD.
quotes: On September 23, 2025, Resolute Holdings transferred the listing of its common stock to the New York Stock Exchange where it continues to trade under the ticker symbol “RHLD”.

material_events.claim: GPGI completed the Husky Transaction under the November 2, 2025 Share Purchase Agreement to combine with Husky Technologies Limited for aggregate consideration of approximately $4.976 billion, making Husky Holdings a wholly owned subsidiary of GPGI Holdings.

The Husky Transaction was completed on January 12, 2026, whereby Husky Holdings became a wholly owned subsidiary of GPGI Holdings.

The Husky Management Agreement has an initial term of 10 years and shall automatically renew for successive ten-year terms unless terminated in accordance with its terms.
